title: HH or HT: which waits?
blocks: Flip a fair coin until you get two heads in a row. Then flip again until you get a head followed by a tail. Same coin, same odds. Which one takes longer? It should be a tie. It isn't.

Here are the rules. Game A: keep flipping until the last two flips are heads-heads. Game B: keep flipping until the last two flips are heads-tails. Count the flips, play many times, and take the average.
At any single spot, both patterns have the same one in four chance. But the averages are different. Heads-tails takes four flips on average. Heads-heads takes six.
Why? Look at heads-tails. Say you've flipped a head. If the next flip is another head, you're not set back. That second head is already the start of a new try. You never fall behind.
Now heads-heads. You flip a head, and then a tail. That tail resets you to zero, and the head you had is wasted. Every failure sends you right back to the start.
Race them. Heads-tails averages about four flips. Heads-heads averages about six.
Both patterns are equally likely at any spot. But heads-heads clumps together, and clumps make you wait. Averages can hide patterns that probabilities don't show.
